summary.title: Recurrent Interpolants for Probabilistic Time Series Prediction
summary.authors: Yu Chen, Marin Biloš, Sarthak Mittal, Wei Deng, Kashif Rasul, Anderson Schneider
summary.executive_summary: This paper addresses the scalability and modeling challenges of probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a novel framework that blends the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models. Traditional autoregressive models, such as RNNs and Transformers, are widely used but often rely on simple parametric output layers (e.g., Gaussian), limiting their ability to capture complex, high-dimensional distributions and cross-feature dependencies. While generative models like Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) and Flow Matching (FM) offer superior distributional modeling, they face scalability issues when applied to long time series windows due to the model size being proportional to both feature dimension and window length. The authors introduce a method based on Stochastic Interpolants (SI), extended to a conditional generation framework with additional control features. The core innovation is the use of an RNN to encode the historical context into a history prompt, which then conditions the SI module to predict the next time step. This approach avoids mapping from pure noise to data, instead mapping from the current time point to the next, leveraging the strong correlations between neighboring time points. Theoretical contributions include extending SI theory to arbitrary joint distributions and conditional generation. Empirically, the method is evaluated on synthetic datasets and four real-world multivariate time series datasets (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki). The proposed SI-based model outperforms or matches baselines (DDPM, SGM, FM, Vec-LSTM) on three out of four datasets in terms of CRPS-sum, demonstrating superior uncertainty quantification and predictive accuracy. The framework offers a computational-friendly alternative for large-scale generative time series prediction.

claims.description: The proposed SI-based framework outperforms or matches existing generative and recurrent baselines in probabilistic time series forecasting.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper addresses the scalability and modeling challenges of probabilistic time series forecasting by proposing a novel framework that blends the computational efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with the high-quality probabilistic modeling of diffusion models. Traditional autoregressive models, such as RNNs and Transformers, are widely used but often rely on simple parametric output layers (e.g., Gaussian), limiting their ability to capture complex, high-dimensional distributions and cross-feature dependencies. While generative models like Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) and Flow Matching (FM) offer superior distributional modeling, they face scalability issues when applied to long time series windows due to the model size being proportional to both feature dimension and window length. The authors introduce a method based on Stochastic Interpolants (SI), extended to a conditional generation framework with additional control features. The core innovation is the use of an RNN to encode the historical context into a history prompt, which then conditions the SI module to predict the next time step. This approach avoids mapping from pure noise to data, instead mapping from the current time point to the next, leveraging the strong correlations between neighboring time points. Theoretical contributions include extending SI theory to arbitrary joint distributions and conditional generation. Empirically, the method is evaluated on synthetic datasets and four real-world multivariate time series datasets (Solar, Exchange, Traffic, Wiki). The proposed SI-based model outperforms or matches baselines (DDPM, SGM, FM, Vec-LSTM) on three out of four datasets in terms of CRPS-sum, demonstrating superior uncertainty quantification and predictive accuracy. The framework offers a computational-friendly alternative for large-scale generative time series prediction.

Research Context
Sequential models like RNNs and Transformers are standard for time series forecasting. These models capture dependencies but are limited by simple probabilistic output layers. Generative models using diffusion or flow-based methods address complex distribution modeling. However, these generative models face scalability issues with large time windows. A computational-friendly framework is needed for large-scale generative predictions.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is how to combine RNN efficiency with diffusion model quality. The hypothesis is that mapping from current to future points is more effective than noise-to-data. The method relies on stochastic interpolants extended to conditional generation. It is predicted that this approach will improve probabilistic forecasting performance. The framework aims to address challenges in high-dimensional complex distributions.

Methodological Details
The study uses synthetic two-dimensional datasets for initial verification. Real-world datasets include Solar, Exchange, Traffic, and Wiki. The model uses an RNN to encode context into a history prompt. Stochastic Interpolants (SI) are used for the generative module. The training uses importance sampling with a Beta distribution. Evaluation metrics include CRPS-sum, NRMSE, and Normalized Deviance. Baselines include DDPM, SGM, FM, and Vec-LSTM. The context window length P is a key parameter.

Procedures And Architectures
The model architecture consists of an RNN and an SI module. The RNN encodes the past context into a history vector. The SI module performs conditional generation from current to next point. The velocity and score functions are modeled by neural networks. Training minimizes mean squared error for velocity and score. Inference involves solving the forward SDE for the next time step. The method supports multi-step prediction via recursive step-by-step forecasting. Hyperparameters were tuned using synthetic datasets first.

Key Results
On the Solar dataset, SI achieved a CRPS-sum of 0.359. On the Exchange dataset, SI achieved a CRPS-sum of 0.007. On the Traffic dataset, FM outperformed SI with a CRPS-sum of 0.038. On the Wiki dataset, SI achieved a CRPS-sum of 0.080. SI outperformed or matched baselines on three out of four datasets. The model captured uncertainty effectively on the Solar dataset. Wasserstein distance metrics confirmed good sample quality on synthetic data.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The method demonstrates that mapping from current to future points is effective. It shows that careful probability distribution modeling is critical. The extension of SI to conditional generation is a theoretical contribution. The approach bridges the gap between RNN efficiency and diffusion quality. It provides insights for future developments in generative time series models.

Contradictions And Limitations
FM performed better than SI on the Traffic dataset. FM failed to capture the data distribution on the Wiki dataset. The paper notes that loss values are larger near the ends of diffusion time. The method requires recursive inference for multi-step predictions. Code availability is pending for the camera-ready version.

Claims
The proposed SI-based framework outperforms or matches existing generative and recurrent baselines in probabilistic time series forecasting. SI achieved the best CRPS-sum on Solar and Exchange datasets. SI outperformed Vec-LSTM on all datasets. The model captured uncertainty well on Solar data. FM achieved a lower CRPS-sum on the Traffic dataset. FM failed on the Wiki dataset. SI is a strong candidate for conditional generation in time series. The framework is suitable for large-scale applications.

Data And Code Availability
The code will be publicly available for the camera-ready version. Real-world datasets are from public sources like UCI and GluonTS.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Different schedulers for SI were tested on synthetic data. Most gamma-interpolant function combinations achieved good results. Importance sampling was used to stabilize training.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 2 illustrates the model diagram with RNN and SI. Figure 3 shows generated samples for synthetic datasets. Figure 4 shows forecast paths on the Solar dataset. Table 1 reports Wasserstein distances for synthetic data. Table 2 reports CRPS-sum metrics for real datasets.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a framework blending RNNs and Stochastic Interpolants. 2. The strongest evidence is superior CRPS-sum on three of four real datasets. 3. The future path involves further development of conditional generative models.
